stories.head: From Found to Cited: Navigating the New Frontier of AI Search
stories.plain: The piece argues that AI agents are now the most important 'visitors' to your website, acting on behalf of real customers. This reframes the entire goal of digital presence: being cited inside an AI answer matters more than ranking in a list of links. Marketers need to rethink content, structure, and authority signals for a generative-engine world.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Introduces Agent Teams via Acquisition of DoubleO.ai
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and launched Agent Teams, a system where coordinated AI agents execute full go-to-market plays — from signal detection to outreach — without human hand-holding at each step. This matters because it moves agentic AI from single-task bots to multi-agent workflows that own an entire sales motion, changing how GTM platforms are bought and evaluated.

stories.head: Braze Expands AI from Content Creation to Campaign Operations
stories.plain: Braze added AI decisioning tools that automate campaign checks and connect its platform to external LLMs like Claude. This shifts Braze from a content-generation helper to an operational layer that decides campaign logic — a meaningful product change that affects how marketers govern and run always-on engagement at scale.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Radically Different 'AI Shelves'
stories.plain: New Jellyfish data shows that AI shopping assistants build their own product shortlists that don't mirror traditional brand rankings or price positioning. Jellyfish launched a 'Share of Model' measurement product in response. This reframes competitive strategy — brands must optimize for AI recommendation logic, not just search rankings or shelf placement.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust™ to Verify Agentic Commerce Intent
stories.plain: Experian and DataDome now continuously verify not just which AI agent is acting, but whether its actions stay within what it was authorized to do throughout a transaction. This is an early piece of governance infrastructure for agentic commerce — exactly the trust layer that procurement and compliance teams will require before allowing autonomous agents to spend money.

stories.head: Salesforce Acquires AI Customer Research Startup Listen Labs
stories.plain: Salesforce bought Listen Labs, whose AI conducts customer interviews, analyses responses, and simulates customer behavior. The plan is to wire this directly into Salesforce CRM and its AI agents. This closes a data gap: agents will soon act on synthesized voice-of-customer insight, not just CRM transaction history, changing what feeds decisioning.

themes.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Discoverability Rules
body: The move from keyword ranking to AI citation is the single biggest structural shift in organic reach this decade. Brands that aren't optimising to be cited by generative engines — not merely indexed — are already losing visibility without knowing it.

Visual SEO, structured content signals, and a deep understanding of how LLMs select sources are now table-stakes skills. The old playbook of backlinks and keyword density doesn't translate cleanly; marketers need a new evidence-of-authority framework built for probabilistic retrieval.
ev: Agile Brand · From Found to Cited
MarTech · Visual SEO for AI Search

themes.head: AI Agents Enter the Commerce Layer
body: Autonomous AI agents are moving beyond productivity tools into revenue-critical workflows: ZoomInfo's Agent Teams acquisition, Growth7's CRM-to-pipeline platform, and DataDome's intent-verification layer in agentic commerce all signal that orchestrated agent stacks are becoming the new GTM infrastructure.

But governance is lagging badly. GTM teams are already losing track of which agents are running, what data they're touching, and who owns their outputs. The companies that build agent-oversight practices now will have a durable advantage over those that let agent sprawl compound.
ev: MarTech · GTM Teams Losing Track of AI Agents

themes.head: Speed Without Quality: AI's Unfinished Promise
body: The data is in: AI made marketing faster first and better only sometimes. Velocity gains in content production have not automatically produced better customer experiences — and rising customer expectations (driven by AI-powered interactions) mean the tolerance gap for mediocre output is shrinking fast.

This creates a strategic inflection point. Teams that use efficiency savings to fund deeper personalisation and creative quality will pull ahead; teams that simply use AI to produce more of the same will erode brand equity. The Mixbook case — deliberately hiding its AI use to focus on emotional permanence — illustrates the counter-intuitive discipline required.
ev: MarTech · Customers Expect More, Tolerate Less
Agile Brand · Mixbook CEO on AI & Permanence

themes.head: The B2B Evidence Crisis Reshapes Buyer Journeys
body: B2B marketing's persistent ROI debate has been reframed: the problem isn't measurement tools, it's the quality and credibility of evidence presented to CFOs and buying committees. AI-shaped buyer journeys mean prospects arrive further along and better informed, demanding proof rather than promises.

CMOs are responding by investing in buyer-intelligence infrastructure — richer intent data, tighter CRM-to-pipeline loops, and content strategies tuned to the questions AI assistants surface during research. Salesforce's acquisition of Listen Labs (AI customer research) and Growth7's CRM-activation platform are direct bets on closing this evidence gap.
ev: Agile Brand · CMO Buyer Intelligence Guide

themes.head: Retail & Physical Media Stage an AI-Powered Comeback
body: Retail media is evolving from digital banner placements to AI-managed, experiential in-store activations. CommerceIQ's expansion to Chewy Ads and Particular Audience's trade-media platform show vendors racing to own the layer between physical shelf presence and algorithmic ad optimisation.

Simultaneously, TV & streaming are being repositioned as full-funnel instruments — not just awareness plays — with Comcast research showing measurable impact across the entire buyer journey. Taken together, these moves signal that the next competitive battleground is the blended physical-digital media mix, not just digital-only performance channels.
ev: MarTech Series · Comcast TV Buyer Journey Research

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — search, agents, content, evidence, and media — the decisive advantage is shifting to teams that govern AI output quality as rigorously as they deploy AI for speed.
